crm_domain.description: Whether this deployment fronts the optional CRM (ADR-0047) under /crm/*, for the terminal's record page.
crm_domain.when_unconfigured: No /crm/* route is registered, so a request there is 404. The CRM's agent tools are the MCP's and absent with it.

agent_domain.description: Whether this deployment fronts the AGENT domain (PRD decision 40.7: meetings, agents and flows work independently and in any configuration, identity being the only shared dependency). Presence is a configuration fact — whether the deployment named the door — never a probe: a probe makes "agent-api is restarting" and "there is no agent-api" the same answer, and the second is a shipped product.
agent_domain.when_unconfigured: The edge registers no /agent/* route and assembles no agent rows into its scope table, so a request to /agent/anything is 404 — this deployment does not serve it — rather than a 401 about a route that is not here. Everything else is unchanged: this is the `no-agents` product of decision 40.6 (gateway + meetings + flows + identity), not a degraded gateway.

flows_service_door.description: This deployment runs a flows tier, and the gateway serves its service door (service_door.py): the only way the flows services reach another domain, and the only way the internal tier reaches flows-api.
flows_service_door.when_unconfigured: No door is served. A deployment without flows needs none; flows itself refuses to start without its key.

subject_tickets.description: The service door binds a flows call that acts for a person to a ticket the producer of that person's fact signed (subject-ticket.v1): meeting-api for a meeting, agent-api for a routine or message, the mail intake for an authenticated invite or reply, this gateway for a person's own bearer.
subject_tickets.when_unconfigured: No producer's ticket verifies, so the door refuses every person-bound flows call (403 subject_ticket_required / subject_ticket_refused) except the ones a gateway ticket opens; unbound and system calls are unchanged. A deployment without flows serves no door and needs no keys.

keys.description: shared internal secret attached as X-Internal-Secret on the admin-api /internal/validate hop (adapters.py:67-69). Unset, admin-api rejects validation and EVERY API-key check 503s (fail-closed) — so the boot refuses instead of coming up green and 503ing every call (the 2026-04-23 failure shape, #526). It is ALSO the internal-tier authority agent-api's _internal_caller and admin-api's _check_internal compare against, which is why a published placeholder is refused outright (F95).

gateway-identity.v1 signing key: a file holding the gateway's Ed25519 PRIVATE key (PKCS#8 PEM). The gateway signs the identity it resolved onto every forward (X-Vexa-Identity, short expiry); agent-api, meeting-api and the credential broker hold only the public half and can verify but never sign. No other service mounts this file. Unset, or not an Ed25519 private key, the boot refuses. Generated at install: compose's identity-keys one-shot, the Helm identity-keys Secret, the Lite entrypoint (persisted in its state directory).
admin-api base URL for the /internal/validate token-resolution hop
meeting-api base URL — the proxy forward target and the /ws/authorize-subscribe hop

agent control-plane base URL; the edge fronts it under /agent/*, forwarded onto its /api/* (routes.v1 `forward`). UNSET MEANS THE AGENT DOMAIN IS NOT DEPLOYED (PRD 40.6 no-agents, 40.7 domains are independent): the edge registers no /agent/* route and assembles no agent rows into its scope table, so a request there is 404 — this deployment does not serve it — rather than a 401 about a route that is not here. A URL default would assert the domain exists and make its absence unsayable.

The optional CRM's base URL (ADR-0047); the edge fronts its read, history and review under /crm/* (routes.v1 `forward`) for the terminal's record page. UNSET MEANS NO CRM IS DEPLOYED: no /crm/* route is registered and a request there is 404.

The flows tier's one credential (service_door.py). Set, this process also listens on VEXA_GATEWAY_SERVICE_DOOR_PORT and forwards exactly the calls on the flows allow-list (FLOWS_OUTBOUND) to agent-api, admin-api, meeting-api and crm-api — over the internal tier, or for meeting-api with the subject's identity signed here with the scopes bot+tx — and refuses everything else with a 403 that never leaves this process. flows-api, flows-worker and flows-mailbox hold the SAME value and no other internal credential: not INTERNAL_API_SECRET, not the admin key. Unset: no door, and this deployment runs no flows tier.

flows-api's base URL (the name flows' mcp.tools.v1 manifest binds for the edge, base_url_env), for the door's inbound leg (/to-flows/*): the signals service's wake and the terminal's sign-in mail present X-Internal-Secret to the door, never to flows, and the door forwards the allow-listed calls (FLOWS_INBOUND) with the flows key.

subject-ticket.v1: the directory of the ticket producers' Ed25519 PUBLIC keys, one SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM per issuer named `<issuer>.pem` (`meetings.pem`, `agent.pem`, `mail.pem`); the `gateway` issuer is this process's own identity key and needs no file. The service door (with VEXA_FLOWS_SERVICE_KEY set) forwards a person-bound flows call (transcript.read, bot.dispatch, chat.autonomous, desk.write, room.bills_to, routine.turn) only when one ticket in X-Vexa-Subject-Ticket verifies under its issuer's key here, is unexpired, lists the class and names the call's subject (and meeting); otherwise 403 subject_ticket_required / subject_ticket_refused / ticket_replayed. Public keys only: the gateway can verify and never sign for meetings, agent or mail. UNSET, or no file for an issuer, that issuer's tickets do not verify. Filled at install from each producer's keypair: compose's subject-ticket-keys one-shot, the Helm subject-ticket-verify-keys ConfigMap.
The service door's own port. No deploy surface publishes it: only the flows tier, the signals service and the terminal reach it, inside the deployment's network.

Comma-separated additional Jitsi deployment hostnames, read by the service door's copy of meeting-api's link parser (fact meeting-link-door) to name the meeting a flows bot dispatch addresses. Set it to the same value meeting-api has; unset ⇒ no extra hosts.

the ONE assembled MCP service (ADR-0037) — the streamable-HTTP transport fronted under /mcp (GET streams the SSE leg, POST forwards buffered). Every bearer reaches it: a person's API key and a worker's delegation token alike

Who the agent tier (every /agent/* row) is enabled for. Empty: everyone a key scope admits (no restriction). '*': everyone. Otherwise a comma-separated list of user ids and/or email addresses, compared without case; an entry starting with '@' admits every address at that domain. A caller it does not name is answered 403 agent_tier_not_enabled before anything is forwarded; a worker's delegation token is admitted by the person it acts for. agent-api reads the same setting the same way.

how /ws holds a key to the REST routes' scopes. strict (default) = opening takes a meeting-status scope and subscribing takes the transcript read's scope (tx); a refused key gets insufficient_scope / close 4403. legacy = an explicit opt-in to the 0.12 contract, a residual: any valid key (a bot-only key included) opens the socket and subscribes to the meetings the authorize hop grants it, logging ws_scope_legacy_allowed when strict would refuse.
